councillors.name: Louise Gibbard
bio: It's been a real honour and privilege to serve as a councillor for Dunvant since 2017, and for the whole of Dunvant and Killay since 2022.

Hopefully, lots of you will know me already; I’m a governor at both Pen Y Fro and Dunvant Primary Schools, Secretary of the Friends of Dunvant Park, have organised lots of community events and I’m a regular litter picker across the area. Away from the ward, I’m the Chair of STOPP (Swansea Takes On Period Poverty), an active member of Unite Community Swansea branch and Joint Cabinet Member for Supporting Communities involved in making Council decisions around things like equalities and human rights, tackling domestic abuse and our community facilities across Swansea.
I’m passionate about public service, and doing my bit to represent local people and working with you to make improvements to our lovely area.

councillors.name: Dai Jenkins
bio: My name is Dai Jenkins and I am excited to be standing in May’s elections as one of the Labour candidates in Gowerton ward.

I live 500 metres from the stream that separates Waunarlwydd from Gowerton and am the fourth generation to live in Waunarlwydd. I have always loved being involved in my local community. I am a member of Waunarlwydd RFC and am one of the organisers of the Waunarlwydd Carnival, which raised around 5K (pre Covid) each year for charity. Married to Michelle for 30 years our daughter Laura-May is a Nurse and our youngest daughter Beth qualifies as a Midwife come July this year. Both Laura and Beth attended Ysgol Gyfun Gwyr.
Over the last 41 years I have worked for B.T and have been a Labour Party member for 30 years. Currently I am a full time Union Officer of the South Wales Branch of the Communication Workers Union.

In 2021 I was active in the “Climate- Change” day of action in Swansea- spoke in Castle square against fire and re-hire contracts, spoke and supported May day’s international workers rally and spoke at “Youth for Jobs” event.

councillors.name: Cyril Anderson
bio: Cyril, elected May 2015, is Swansea born & bred with strong roots in the ward. He is a school governor on both Seaview & Townhill primary schools, and he works closely with community & charity groups, and is very vocal when it comes to speaking out on behalf of local Issues.

He is very keen on providing opportunities for children, such as the new play areas that have been constructed at Mayhill Park. But he is equally keen to help support the elderly and the vulnerable, and has always been actively involved in TOPIC House, the Older People's Information Centre.
He chairs the Economy, Environment & Infrastructure Policy Development Committee which helps to achieve the aims of the council.
Cyril has been an activist in the Labour Party for well over 15 years, and a union man for many years, and is married.

councillors.name: David Hopkins
bio: David, who is also Swansea born & bred, has been a councillor representing this ward for over 30 years and is well known across the ward. He served as the Lord Mayor of Swansea for 16-17, and now shares the demanding roles of both Deputy Leader, as well as being the Cabinet Member for Delivery.

He is also currently governor at Townhill primary school. He has always dealt with ward issues as a priority and works hard behind the scenes to get things done, such as securing additional funding to replace the All Weather Pitch at the Phoenix Centre, and ensure funding for the construction of the new play areas on Mayhill Park.
He has been a member of the Labour Party for over 40 years, and a member of Unite union. David is married with 3 three grown up children and three grandchildren.

councillors.name: Lesley Walton
bio: Lesley got elected in 2012 and has been a school governor ever since, at Seaview Primary and currently at Dylan Thomas Community School. Knowing the issues which face the ward she is keen to promote the local Swansea Bay Credit Union, where members can borrow at a reasonable interest, & save money.
She has also been particularly involved in the setting up of the Friends of Mayhill Washing Lake & Community Food Garden, to address flytipping issues and provide communal food.
As Diversity Champion she speaks up at committee meetings, on social media, and uses her house front window to promote events. She is looking forward to helping Swansea become a Human Rights City.
She has been a Labour Party & union member, currently Unite, for over 35 years. Lesley is married with two cats, and runs her own design & print business.

councillors.name: Rebecca Fogarty
bio: An active member of the community since moving here in 2016, I am Vice Chair of Mumbles Community Council and a Governor at Mayals Primary School. I am active in a local church and volunteer on local environmental projects.

I have varied work experience in the public and charity sectors. I now work in public health so it’s been a busy couple of years for me! I led the local community council response to the first wave of the Covid-19 pandemic, ensuring all residents had access to essential food and prescriptions.

As a new Mam, you’ll often see me out with the pram. I want all generations in West Cross to enjoy good physical and mental well-being. I believe in involving people and bringing the community together to improve our local area. I’ve enjoyed talking to residents about varied issues, and look forward to meeting you in the near future.

councillors.name: Sara Keeton
bio: I’m a Mumbles Community Councillor and Chair of the Environmental Committee; also, I chair West Cross Community Centre Management Committee. I'm a School Governor at The Grange and YGG Llwynderw.

Living in West Cross nearly all my life, I've spent many years raising my family here. I have volunteered at local schools and with mental health and learning disability organisations over the years. I ran a business with my husband and my current work places me in the heart of the community.

I love West Cross and want it to remain a safe and fun place to be, to grow up and to grow older! Our fabulous community benefits from Mumbles and Gower being so close and still has strong links with the rest of Swansea. I want more opportunities for our residents to enjoy being part of what's on offer and to create more local interest groups, clubs and socials.
